text: I scoped this to roughly 376-476 CE, from the Gothic crossing of the Danube to the deposition of the last western emperor. Historians disagree about decline versus transformation, so the causes are layered rather than ranked.

block.title: How the Western Roman Empire fell
block.because: You asked to understand the fall of the Western Roman Empire

sections.md: The Western Roman Empire stopped functioning as a state over the fifth century CE [E]. The conventional end date is 476, when [[Odoacer|person]] deposed [[Romulus Augustulus|person]] [E], though real power had long passed to generals and Germanic kingdoms [E]. No single cause explains it [L].

The empire was administered as two halves, and after [[Theodosius I|person]] died in 395 it was never again ruled by one emperor [E]. The West was poorer and had longer, more exposed frontiers than the East [L]. After the Goths crossed the Danube in 376 and destroyed a Roman army at [[Adrianople|event]] in 378 [E], Rome increasingly settled armed groups inside its borders instead of expelling them [E]. The [[Vandals|term]] took Carthage in 439, cutting the West off from its richest tax base in North Africa [E]; many historians see this as the point of no return [L].

Successor kingdoms took over Roman territory: Visigoths in Iberia, Franks in Gaul, Ostrogoths in Italy [E]. Many kept Roman law, Latin and the Church as working institutions [E]. The Eastern Roman Empire, centred on [[Constantinople|place]], continued until 1453 [E].

Older accounts, following [[Edward Gibbon|person]], told this as decline and fall [E]. From the 1970s, historians such as [[Peter Brown|person]] stressed transformation into a new world of late antiquity, while others such as [[Bryan Ward-Perkins|person]] argue the archaeology shows a real collapse in living standards [C].

edges.why: Rule by several emperors became the normal answer to an empire too large for one court.
Mistreatment of the Gothic refugees led to revolt and a pitched battle.
With its eastern field army destroyed, Rome negotiated rather than expelled the Goths.
An armed Gothic people inside the empire gave Alaric a base for his demands on Rome.
The West had to defend Africa with fewer resources and little eastern help.
Losing African taxes and grain left the West unable to pay its armies.
The sack was a huge shock, but how much it weakened the state is debated.
Odoacer's deposition of Romulus Augustulus marked, rather than caused, the end.
Theodoric replaced Odoacer and ruled Italy with Roman institutions intact.
The East still saw the West as Roman land and tried to recover it.
The richer, more defensible East could survive the shocks that broke the West.

block.title: Meanwhile in India
block.because: Simultaneity: what else was happening in the same decades
block.md: While the Western Empire fragmented, the [[Gupta Empire|place]] in northern India was near its height under [[Chandragupta II|person]], who reigned from about 375 to 415 [L].
